IS : 7473 - 1974

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR BRUSHES, TAR
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard war, adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 November 1974, after the draft finalized by the Brushware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 Considerable assistance has been taken from IND/GS/359 (C) ' Brushes, tar ' issued by the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for tar brushes. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 5060-1969 and the one given below shall apply. 2.1.1 Approved Tender Sample -- The sample accepted by the indentor or inspection authority as the basis of supply. When a sample is tested and approved by the purchaser or an inspection authority, the results of such tests as will permit the supplier to meet the limits imposed by the specification for deliveries, shall be made available to the supplier. 3. GRADES AND TYPES 3.1 Grades -- Tar brushes shall be of two grades, namely: a) Grade 1 -- With bristles as filling material, and b) Grade 2 -- With 50 percent coco fibre and 50 percent horse-tail hair as filling material.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )Glossary of terms used in brushware industry.

3

IS : 7473 - 1974 3.2 T y p e s -- Each grade of tar brushes shall be of the following two types: a) Type 1 -- Long handle tar brushes, and b) Type 2 Short handle tar brushes.

4. REQUIREMENTS 4.1 M a t e r i a l s 4.1.1 Filling Materials -- For Grade 1 tar brushes, the filling material shall be grey bristles. T h e bristles used shall be properly straightened, cleaned, freed from adulterants and shall conform to I S : 1844-1962*. As regards colour, lustre and stiffness, the bristles shall match those used in the approved tender sample. 4.1.1.1 For Grade 2 tar brushes, the filling material shall be 50 percent coco fibre and 50 percent horse-tail hair. 4.1.2 Timber 4.1.2.1 Any of the timber species listed in Appendix A shall be used in the manufacture of the wooden portion of the brush. 4.1.2.2 T h e timber shall be reasonably straight-grained and wellseasoned to a moisture content not exceeding 15 percent when tested by the electronic moisture meter method. In case of dispute, the oven dry method shall be used ( see Appendix B ). 4.1.2.3 T h e timber shall be free from brashness, any kind of biological or non-biological deterioration, insect attack, centre heart ( pith ), knots ( except pin knots ), cracks, warp and any other defects which may reduce the life of the brush or affect its utility. 4.1.3 Ferrule -- The ferrule shall be made of 0.60 to 0.80 mm thick mild steel either seamless or lapped and brazed or welded or riveted. 4.1.4 Cement -- Any suitable specified under 7 may be used. cement capable of satisfying the tests

4.1.4.1 Vulcanized rubber setting may be used subject to agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 4.1.5 Varnish, Black and Varnish, Shellac 4.1.6 Plug and Pin -- Wooden plug and pin of shape and dimensions as shown in Fig. 1 shall be used.
*Specification for bristles.

4

IS : 7473 - 1974 4.2 D i m e n s i o n s a n d T o l e r a n c e s 4.2.1 Dimensions -- T h e brushes of Type I and Type 2 shall conform to the dimensions given in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 respectively. 4.2.2 Tolerances -- T h e tolerance on the linear dimensions shall be as follows: Naminal Dimension Tolerance mm mm Up to 15 � 1.0 Over 15 but below 40 � 2.0 40 and above � 3.0 4.2.2.1 The solid dressing of the bristles used shall be in accordance with Table 1 of IS : l844-1962*. 4.3 M a n u f a c t u r e 4.3.1 For Type 1 Brushes 4.3.1.1 The brushes shall conform to the shape and design as shown in Fig. 1. 4.3.1.2 The ferrule shall be seamless or lapped and brazed or welded or riveted. 4.3.1.3 T h e handle shall be tightly hinged with the plug which in turn is tightly fitted in the ferrule. 4.3.2 For Type 2 Brushes 4.3.2.1 The brushes shall conform to the shape and design shown in Fig. 2. 4.3.2.2 T h e handle shall tightly fit in the ferrule. 4.4 W o r k m a n s h i p and F i n i s h 4.4.1 T h e wooden portion of the brush shall be finished smooth all over and shall be properly varnished or lacquered. 4.4.2 In general workmanship and finish, the brushes shall match the approved ender sample. 4.5 P r e s e r v a t i o n -- The filling material of the brushes shall be liberally dusted with a mixture of 5 parts ( by mass ) of D D T dusting powder (see IS : 564-1964 ) and 95 percent ( b y mass) of French chalk (see IS: 380-1967). *Specification for bristles. Specification for DDT dusting powders ( revised ). Specification for French chalk, technical (first revision ).

IS : 7473 - 1974 5 . PACKING A N D M A R K I N G 5.1 P a c k i n g -- T h e packing shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier but shall be such as to ensure retention of the preservative. 5.2 M a r k i n g -- Unless otherwise agreed to between the indentor or the inspection authority and the supplier, each brush shall be legibly marked or stamped with the manufacturer's name or recognized trade-mark, if any, grade, type and the year of manufacture. 5.2.1 The product may also be marked with Standard mark. The use of the Siandard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thercunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for thc use of Siandard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

6. SAMPLING 6.1 T h e method of sampling of tar brushes and the criteria for conformity shall be as prescribed in Appendix C. 7. T E S T S 7.1 P u l l T e s t -- T h e cement shall not fail when a small bunch of filling material is subjected to a straight pull with t h u m b and finger grip. 7.2 O v e n T e s t 7.2.1 For Non-rubber Set Brushes -- T h e brush without handle, when suspended in an oven with the protruding filling material end upward and subjected to a temperature of 60 � 2�C for 4 hours, shall show no appreciable creeping of the cement and after cooling in the atmosphere for 30 minutes, the cement shall satisfy the pull test prescribed in 7.1 . 7.2.2 For Rubber Set Brushes -- T h e brush without handle, when suspended in an oven with the protruding filling material end upward and subjected to a temperature of 132 � 2�C for two hours, shall show no creeping of the cement and after cooling in the atmosphere for 30 minutes, the cement shall satisfy the pull test prescribed under 7.1 . 7.3 M a s s of Filling Material per Finished Brush 7.3.1 Remove the handle, ferrule, binding, staples, etc, from the brush by mechanical means. These can be removed from pitch-set fillings after

8

IS : 7473 - 1974 softening of the setting. Soak the setting medium, if any, in an appropriate solvent until it is sufficiently friable to be broken down. 7.3.1.1 Break down the setting by rubbing it between the fingers and hammering it lightly, these processes being carried out over a large sheet of paper and repeated at intervals of about 15 minutes until all the setting medium has been removed. 7.3.1.2 Nails, pins, wedges, etc, may be removed at any convenient stage. 7.3.1.3 Spread all the filling material, including any pieces broken off in the above process, in a thin layer on a sheet of paper, to allow the solvent to evaporate. 7.3.2 The total mass of the filling material per brush shall be 99 g and 70 g for Type 1 and Type 2 brushes respectively. A tolerance of � 5 percent shall be allowed on the mass of filling material. The mass of filling material in a lot shall be assessed by taking the average mass of three brushes in lots not exceeding 300 brushes and of six brushes in lots exceeding 300 brushes but not exceeding 500.

APPENDIX B
( Clause 4.1.2.2)
D E T E R M I N A T I O N OF M O I S T U R E C O N T E N T OF TIMBER U S E D IN TAR BRUSHES B-1. TEST SPECIMEN B-1.1 T h e entire block used in tar brushes may form the test specimen for the determination of moisture content or a coupon cut from the test specimen may be used for moisture determination. When for any reason additional determination of moisture content is required, separate sample shall be prepared from the sample material as is used in preparing the test specimens. Smaller specimens may be used when deemed necessary. T h e test shall be carried out immediately after cutting the specimen. B.2. P R O C E D U R E B-2.1 Scrape off the paint/varnish from the test specimen and weigh accurately each test specimen. This specimen shall then be dried in a ventilated oven at a temperature of 105 � 2�C until the mass becomes constant between two successive weighings made at an Interval of not less than one hour. B . 3 . CALCULATION B-3.1 T h e moisture content, expressed as a percentage of the oven-dry mass where W 1 = initial mass in g of the test specimen, and W 0 = oven-dry mass in g of the test specimen.

APPENDIX C
( Clause 6.1 )
SAMPLING A N D CRITERIA F O R CONFORMITY OF TAR BRUSHES C-1. SCALE OF SAMPLING C-1.1 L o t -- In a single consignment all brushes of the same type and grade, having the same dimensions and belonging to the same batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot.

11

IS : 7473 - 1974
C-1.1.1 For ascertaining conformity of brushes in a lot to the specified requirements, sampling and testing shall be done for each lot separately. C-1.1.2 The number of brushes to be selected from a lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with Table 1.
TABLE 1 SCALE OF SAMPLING AND PERMISSIBLE NUMBER OF DEFECTIVES
No. OF BRUSHES IN THE LOT SAMPLE SIZE ACCEPTANCE NUMBER

(1)
Up to 50 51 to 100 101 ,, 150 151 ,, 300 301 ,, 500 501 ,, 800 801 ,, 1 000 1 001 and above

(2) 3 5 8 13 20 32 50 80

(3) 0 0 1 2 3 5 8 10

C-1.1.2.1 The brushes to be selected from the lot shall be chosen at random. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, procedures given in IS : 4905-1968* may be followed. C-2. NUMBER OF TESTS C-2-1 All the brushes selected under C-1.1.2 shall be examined for constructional requirements given in 4. Any brush not conforming to any one or more of these requirements shall be considered as defective. C-2.2 All the brushes selected under C-1.1.2 shall be subjected to pull test ( 7 . 1 ) , oven test ( 7 . 2 ) , and mass of filling material per finished brush ( 7.3 ). Any brush failing to pass any one of these tests shall be considered as defective. C-3 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY C-3.1 The lot shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements of the specification if the number of defective brushes found in the sample does not exceed the corresponding acceptance number given in col 3 of the Table 1. *Methods for random sampling. 12
